newsitem.title: REPUBLIC OF IRELAND: PRESS DIGEST - Ireland - September 26.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Ireland - September 26.

text.p: Following are the highlights of stories reported in the Irish press on Thursday.
- Sinn Fein president Gerry Adams has cancelled his planned visit to the Hous of Commons.
- The Revenue Commissioners say there is no chance of collecting all of the almost two billion Irish pounds in unpaid taxes identified in the annual report of the Comptroller and Auditor General.

- The Central Bank has sold large amounts of pounds over the past three days in an attempt to prevent a revaluation of the EU "green pound" and a consequent reduction in the value of EU subsidies to farmers.
- The biggest ever Irish Lotto jackpot of 4.74 million punts was won last night by a ticket bought in Dublin earlier in the afternoon.
- British prime minister John Major last night offered a step-by-step plan for the handover of terrorist weapons that could bring Sinn Fein into the multi-party talks.
- The self-employed and large companies are responsible for most of the 1.9 billion Irish pounds in outstanding unpaid taxes, revealed in the annual report of the Comptroller and Auditor General.

- Millstreet Equestrian Services Ltd, the firm set up by Cork entrepreneur Noel C. Duggan and which stages the Millstreet International Horse Shows, has had its latest accounts qualified by its auditors.
